tier_reason: Tier B stands (independent speedata benchmark with public inputs), but the headline is a wall-clock figure that mixes thread counts: the 500-page document uses pagebreak() between letters, which lets Typst 0.12+ lay out page runs in parallel, while pdflatex is single-threaded. Total CPU time (user plus sys) for 500 pages is 308 ms for Typst against 716 ms for pdflatex, about 2.3x rather than 4.55x, and the marginal per-page CPU is about 1.9x (derived from page data). Typst's speed is version-sensitive: open regressions #7102 (0.13 at 200 ms versus 0.14-rc1 at 1.5 s), #8611 (0.15.0 at 14 minutes and 41 GB versus 0.14.2 at 1 min 17 s and 32 GB) and #8561 (50 s font scan).

corrections.claimed_speedup: speedata benchmark (MacBook Air M4 16 GB, Typst 0.14.2), wall clock: 500 pages Typst 156.6 ms vs pdflatex 712.3 ms (4.55x), LuaLaTeX 2.356 s (15.04x), FOP 1.607 s (10.27x), speedata sp 4.354 s (27.80x), WeasyPrint 8.672 s (55.38x); 1 page: Typst 105.7 ms vs pdflatex 329.1 ms (3.1x, derived), LuaLaTeX 518.6 ms (4.9x, derived); speedata sp fastest at 94.5 ms. The 500-page wall-clock ratio includes Typst's parallel page-run layout against single-threaded pdflatex: total CPU time is 308 vs 716 ms (about 2.3x) and the marginal per-page CPU ratio about 1.9x (derived from page data).
